topic: Ollama llmwatch: Live Prefill Progress Monitoring

key_points: The subject of the review: MIT-licensed Python TUI, created 2026-08-16, last push 2026-08-21, 4 stars / 0 forks / 0 open issues, 13 closed issues (GitHub API, 2026-10-01)
Zero runtime dependencies, Python 3.9+, two entry points: `ollama-llmwatch` and `llmwatch` (package name is `ollama-llmwatch` because `llmwatch` was taken on PyPI)
Reads Ollama's own server log passively with tail -F; never calls the Ollama API and never touches the request path, so it adds no inference overhead

Live board: PREFILL/GENERATE tok/s peak-avg-low with sparklines, cache reuse %, TTFT min/avg/max, WAIT bar (share of session spent reading), SYSTEM swap warning, per-request recent table, live progress bar with ETA

Projection trick: the server only writes a progress line every 512 tokens (5-10s apart), so position is projected from the last measured rate and repainted ~10x/second, clamped so the bar never claims work that hasn't happened

Diagnostic hints instead of raw numbers: '! cache gone - rereading all 39,528 tok', '! same prompt 5x - likely stuck', '! 3 cancels in a row - client keeps timing out', '! slow: 40 vs 100 tok/s usual - 2 models loaded (34 GB), swapping'
--proxy mode (port 8081) for OpenAI-compatible servers (mlx-lm, LM Studio, vLLM) whose logs carry no counts; llama.cpp is the documented exception and uses --log instead
History in SQLite at ~/.local/share/ollama-llmwatch/history.db ('requests' + 'turns' tables); stores timings, model names and effort levels, deliberately no column that could hold prompt text
CLI back-end: --plain, --last, --json, --codex, --history --days N, --turns --days N, --compare A B, --export csv, --no-history, --debug-unparsed

Deliberately does not show CPU/GPU percentage: 'those numbers don't move when performance does' - the GPU sits pinned near 100% whether you get 13 tok/s or 8, so slowdowns are detected from measured throughput instead
Closest direct competitor: Rust, GPLv3, ~17 stars, one static binary, zero runtime deps, explicitly branded 'the local-inference observability layer for your terminal' (GitHub API, 2026-10-01)
Auto-discovers local inference servers and scrapes their metrics endpoints with no config: llama.cpp / vLLM / TGI Prometheus /metrics plus Ollama /api/ps
Shows live generation AND prefill tok/s, KV-cache pressure, queue depth, TTFT - and adds tokens/sec/watt by fusing throughput with GPU power draw
`toptop --diagnose` prints a pasteable 72-column verdict ('MEMORY-BANDWIDTH BOUND - bandwidth 92% / compute 24%'); Ollama users get 'MODEL PARTLY ON CPU' or 'MODEL RUNNING ON CPU' verdicts
Prometheus/JSON export and a long-running :9709 /metrics endpoint for Grafana; multi-host fleet view over SSH

The key contrast: toptop reads the HTTP metrics endpoints, llmwatch reads the log - so toptop sees KV/queue/TTFT and GPU state but cannot see in-flight prefill progress or per-request cache accounting the way the log parser can

Prometheus metrics sidecar for Ollama: a transparent reverse proxy that forwards to Ollama and exposes token usage, request duration, inference speed, model memory and load status (~42 stars, last push 2025-06-24)
Zero configuration, no modification to Ollama, ships a pre-built Grafana dashboard, env vars OLLAMA_HOST / PORT, Docker image ghcr.io/norskhelsenett/ollama-metrics
Represents the 'proxy meter' category: it only knows about requests that go through it, and only learns numbers at response time - the silent prefill window is invisible to it

Local LLM Observatory: full observability interface for Ollama - chat, streaming, reasoning, RAG, introspection, metrics; Apache-2.0, ~8 stars, npm package `llmxray` v0.6.0, 395 downloads in the last month

Its maintainer published the definitive write-up on Ollama 0.33.3 breaking the standard prefill-throughput formula, and ships a page that measures cache reuse against your live daemon rather than estimating it
Browser-based (express + dexie + vue), so it is a dashboard rather than a terminal companion; llmwatch's lane is the always-on terminal pane next to your agent
'add /metrics endpoint' opened 2024-03-14, still open, 140 reactions and 48 comments - the most-wanted observability request in the Ollama repo

Two competing implementations are open right now: PR #16998 (2026-07-01, opt-in GET /metrics under OLLAMA_METRICS=1, scheduler gauges + ollama_prompt_eval_total, +936/-50 in 13 files) and PR #18508 (2026-09-17, +407 in 4 files, self-described as an alternative rather than a replacement)
Until one lands, there is no supported server-side metrics endpoint, which is exactly why log-readers like llmwatch exist

Adjacent category - run-level attribution rather than live inference telemetry: ~758 stars, breaks each coding-agent task into work steps (tools used, files changed, tests run, time and tokens) in a local-first dashboard, no login/telemetry
Sits next to agentacct/tokentelemetry (~374 stars, token telemetry across Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI) and Langfuse/LangSmith/Helicone for cloud LLM observability
Useful framing for the post: cost-and-token meters answer 'what did this cost me', llmwatch answers 'why is this request slow right now' - different questions, different data sources

stats.fact: Ollama 0.33.3 was released 2026-09-02; it added prompt_eval_cached_count to /api/generate and /api/chat and redefined prompt_eval_duration to cover only the uncached prompt tokens, while prompt_eval_count still means the total prompt size

Because of that redefinition, the standard formula prompt_eval_count / prompt_eval_duration now divides total tokens by the time for only some of them; the error scales with cache-hit ratio. In one measured example the naive formula reported 4375 tok/s where the honest figure was 115 tok/s - a 38x over-report, with no error or warning

The documented fix is to divide by prompt_eval_count - prompt_eval_cached_count; Ollama's own Metrics.Summary() was changed to do exactly this, and prompt_eval_cached_count is declared as a nullable *int in api/types.go (PromptEvalCachedCount *int, omitempty), so 'absent' means unknown rather than zero

KV-cache reuse is prefix-ordered and all-or-nothing from the first divergent token. Same model, same 324-token system prompt, one 21-token timestamp moved from the top to the bottom: prefill fell from 64.6 ms to 18.6 ms with identical wording - 3.5x, from layout alone

Ollama exposes the same cache fact under three different names: native prompt_eval_cached_count; OpenAI-compatible usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens; Anthropic-compatible usage.cache_read_input_tokens - and the Anthropic-compatible input_tokens quietly changed to mean total-minus-cached (identical prompt reported input_tokens 38 cold vs 1 warm)

ollama-llmwatch README's own worked example: a coding agent sends 30,000-55,000 tokens of instructions every turn, which on an M1 Max running a 27B model is roughly eight minutes of silent reading before a single character appears, while the answer itself takes about twenty seconds

The tool's headline metric is the WAIT bar - the share of a session spent in prefill rather than generation; its own sample board shows 91% of session time spent in prefill across 12 requests / 18m04s

Speculative decoding acceptance is workload-dependent, not uniformly good: measured on one M1 Max with the same model and three prompts, code/structured output 58-81% (1.5x faster), rote output/lists 93% (2x), freeform prose 18% (0.6x - slower than no drafter at all)
Turn time can dwarf request time and is dominated by reasoning effort: same model, same machine, 57.3s median turn at low effort vs 33m29s at high effort (n=6 and n=5) - roughly a 35x difference

Generation speed is bandwidth-bound and model-size-bound on an M1 Max: 27B at Q4 10-17 tok/s, 14B at Q4 25-30 tok/s, MoE models such as Qwen3-30B-A3B much higher because only a fraction of weights are read per token

PyPI release skew, verified 2026-10-01: the latest published version is 0.9.1 (uploaded 2026-08-18) with a ~7.6 KB sdist-era footprint, while the GitHub repo's CHANGELOG and README badge already describe 0.9.2 (the package split into llmwatch/ modules with llmwatch.py regenerated by tools/bundle.py). Published versions: 0.5.1, 0.5.2, 0.5.3, 0.6.0, 0.7.0, 0.9.1 - 0.8.0 shipped to GitHub and never reached PyPI at all
Adoption is very early: 4 GitHub stars, 0 forks, 0 subscribers, 0 open issues; PyPI downloads 84 in the last month / 25 in the last week / 0 in the last day (as of 2026-10-01)
Platform support is asymmetric and the author says so: developed and verified on macOS; Linux (journald) and Docker paths are 'written but unverified'; Windows is not supported
Ollama's own log locations, which the tool depends on: macOS ~/.ollama/logs/server.log; Linux with systemd journalctl -u ollama; Docker stdout/docker logs; Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log

The log format llmwatch parses is internal and unstable - every line is tagged with a slot and task id, e.g. 'slot print_timing: id 0 | task 2313 | prompt processing, n_tokens = 4096, progress = 0.27' - and Ollama offers no stability guarantee; the tool ships tests against real captured logs (tests/fixtures/*.log) to catch drift

Ollama still has no server metrics endpoint: issue #3144 ('add /metrics endpoint') has been open since 2024-03-14 with 140 reactions and 48 comments; the two open implementations are PR #16998 (2026-07-01, OLLAMA_METRICS=1, +936/-50 in 13 files) and PR #18508 (2026-09-17, +407 in 4 files)

Streaming prefill progress has been proposed upstream and stalled: PR #13901 'runner: Adds prompt_eval_progress argument to stream prompt completion progress with ollama streaming API' was opened 2026-01-25 and is still open with 0 comments, described by its author as a messy proof of concept

Cache-related prefill defects are active on Ollama's tracker: #16051 (open) MLX bf16 cold prefill is 60-400x slower than warm even when the model fits in RAM; #18505 (open) MLX nvfp4 requests stall in prefill at processed=total-1 for minutes under single-slot load; #18267 (closed) prefix-cache restore truncated to a multiple of 8192 cost a fixed 17-27s re-prefill after every cold prompt; #17829 (closed) MLX had no prompt caching between requests, i.e. full re-prefill every agent step

Ollama's ecosystem scale explains why a niche prefill tool matters: ollama/ollama 181,999 stars and 18,062 forks, llama.cpp 130,029 stars, vLLM 93,031 stars; latest Ollama releases v0.35.0 (2026-09-28) and v0.40.0-rc0 (2026-09-25)

Prefill throughput is an active community obsession in r/LocalLLaMA, which is the tool's natural audience: recent threads include 'PFlash: 10x prefill speedup over llama.cpp at 128K on a RTX 3090', 'TurboQuant isn't just for KV: Qwen3.5-27B... finally fitting on my 16GB 5060 Ti' and '2.5x faster inference with Qwen 3.6 27B using MTP'

The prompt-cache measurement lesson the maintainer of llmxray learned the hard way: comparing whether layout B reuses layout A's cache is the wrong question, because real traffic sends the same layout every turn with a fresh value - each layout has to be sent twice, once with its own values and once with them changed, and only the second send counts

angles: The core gap the tool exists to fill: during prefill, Ollama's API sends nothing at all - no token, no progress, no usage object - so every wire-level and API-level monitor is structurally blind to the window where most of the wall-clock time goes. The server log is the only place the information exists.

The measurement trap is the strongest unique insight: since Ollama 0.33.3, prompt_eval_duration covers only the uncached tokens while prompt_eval_count still counts the whole prompt, so the formula everyone has always used over-reports prefill throughput by the cache-hit ratio - 38x in one measured case, and exactly at its worst in the steady state developers actually care about.

Cache-hit accounting is the real cost model locally: KV reuse is prefix-ordered and all-or-nothing from the first divergent token, so moving a 21-token timestamp from the top of a 324-token prompt to the bottom changed prefill by 3.5x. Hosted providers document the advice to put stable content first; locally you get zero feedback about whether you are following it.

Turn time is not request time and the gap is enormous: the same model on the same machine takes 57.3s at low reasoning effort and 33m29s at high. A tool that only reports per-request tok/s is answering the wrong question for an agent user.

Honest review verdict material: llmwatch is genuinely novel in category but very early - 4 stars, 84 downloads last month, macOS-verified only, Linux unverified, Windows unsupported, PyPI still on 0.9.1 while GitHub describes 0.9.2, and it depends on an internal log format that Ollama does not promise to keep stable.

Category taxonomy worth drawing for readers: log readers (llmwatch) vs metrics scrapers (toptop reading /api/ps and Prometheus) vs proxy meters (ollama-metrics, llmwatch --proxy) - each answers a different question, and only the log reader can show in-flight prefill progress and per-request cache accounting.

Upstream context that makes the post timely: Ollama has had no /metrics endpoint since issue #3144 in March 2024 (140 reactions, 48 comments), two competing Prometheus PRs are open right now, and a streaming prefill-progress PR has sat uncommented since January 2026 - so the whole category is working around a missing server feature.

The 'why is my local model slow' answer most people get wrong: generation is memory-bandwidth-bound and mostly not fixable by tuning flags, while prefill is usually the bigger cost and entirely fixable by shrinking the prompt - the tool's WAIT line is the diagnostic that tells you which problem you actually have.

Speculative decoding as a cautionary tale: acceptance rates of 93% on boilerplate and 18% on prose mean the same drafter can make you 2x faster or 0.6x slower, and measuring acceptance per workload is the only way to know which you are getting.
